full_judgment:
Kazi AT Manowaruddin J: This Rule under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 1-7 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 25-3-2001 (Annexure-B to the petition) passed by the Additional District Judge, Court No. 2, Jessore in Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 23 of 1990 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority. 

 2. The petitioner's case, in short, is that one Mosammat Nurjahan Begum mother and predecessor of the petitioner, filed Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 23 of 1990 before the learned District Judge, Jessore under section 35 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 for setting aside an order passed by the Administrator of Waqf under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance in Office Diary No. 5060 dated 5-2-1989 in relation to EC No. 4474 relating to Tariqullah Biswas Waqf Estate wherein the Waqf Administrator held said Nurjahan Begum a tenant (bharatia) under the Tariqullah Waqf Estate and declared that the case property is the Waqf property of said Waqf Estate. 

 4. In elaborating his first ground Mr Rahman submits that the Additional District Judge has passed the impugned judgment and order without jurisdiction inasmuch as section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance provides that to challenge any order passed under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance a petition has to be filed before the District Judge and the. miscellaneous petition had been so filed before the District Judge and he argues that the Waqf Ordinance being special statute the District Judge alone shall hear the petition, he has no authority to transfer the petition to the Additional District Judge for hearing and disposal. 

 5. Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No 6, submits that the District Judge has the jurisdiction to transfer the case to the Additional District Judge for hearing and disposal. He argues that in said Ordinance the District Judge is not a persona designata but a Court and being a Court he can transfer the matter to the Additional District Judge for hearing and disposal. In support of his contention he referred to quite a few decisions eg (1) Farrukh Ahmed vs Nazir Ahmed alias Badsha Mia 25 DLR (AD) 225, (2) AKM Ruhul Amin vs District Judge and Appellate Election Tribunal, Bhola and others 38 DLR (AD) 172, (3) Amir Sultan Ali Hyder vs Md K Alam alias SAlam and others 29 DLR (AD) 295, (4) Md Younus AIi and another vs Dr M Muslimuddin 1983 BLD, 161 and (5) Syed Abdul Awal and another vs Dewan Abdul Monaem and another 11 DLR 414. 

 6. Admittedly, the Administrator of Waqfs passed the order under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance against which Miscellaneous Case was filed before the District Judge.

 17. From the above definition it is crystal clear that the appeal as contemplated in section 43 could be heard and disposed of by an Additional District Judge and no illegality has been committed in this case because the same has been so disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Chittagong. This view of ours is also supported in the case of Syed Abdul Awal and another vs Dewan Abdul Monaem and another 11 DLR 414 by Akbar and Khan, J. In view of the above we hold that there is no substance in this contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner".
